items.headline: Kalshi Users Under 21 Lost $8.9M in NYC, Probe Finds
items.excerpt: Bloomberg’s J.J. McCorvey joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” Over 50,000 people between the ages of 18 and 21 are using Kalshi in New York City, and they are losing money at a disproportionate rate, according to internal data that Kalshi released to the New York City Council.

The platform has over 100 assets available

items.headline: Focused on Digital Shares Over Tokens: Cunningham
items.excerpt: Stacey Cunningham, president of Bullish and former president of the New York Stock Exchange, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss her recent move to Bullish, market volatility, and her preference of digital shares of tokens. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond
items.excerpt: A federal magistrate judge ordered that the OpenAI staffer charged with bugging a company office conference room be released on a $1 million bond, finding that prosecutors have not presented enough evidence of wrongdoing to keep him in custody.

items.headline: Bitcoin Sinks Below $60,000 Amid ETF Outflows
items.excerpt: Bloomberg Intelligence’s James Seyffart joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” Bitcoin is set to have its eighth straight week of losses, which would be the longest weekly losing streak since 2022. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Nvidia Is a ‘Good Corporate Citizen,’ Attorney General Says
items.excerpt: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Nvidia Corp. is “a good corporate citizen,” while declining to directly answer questions about whether the Justice Department is scrutinizing the circumstances that led to the temporary exit of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

items.headline: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Staff in Employee Meeting
items.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang apologized to employees for the conduct that led to his brief ouster, telling staff at an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that he had let them down, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.headline: CoreWeave Bonds Hit All-Time Lows, Erasing Nvidia-Fueled Gains
items.excerpt: Bonds backing cloud computing provider CoreWeave Inc. fell to record lows Tuesday, among the day’s biggest corporate bond losses, amid renewed concerns about the durability of the AI trade.

items.headline: Tech Slides as Nvidia, AI Risks Take Center Stage

items.excerpt: StoneX senior semiconductor research analyst Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia to Buy with a $270 price target following Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, saying his reinstatement removes key uncertainties around Nvidia’s technology roadmap, industry relationships and support for the AI buildout. items.headline: Nvidia's Huang to Face Bipartisan Scrutiny on Capitol Hill
items.excerpt: Newly reinstated Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer Jensen Huang will testify publicly before a powerful Senate committee on Dec. 3, according to a statement from the panel’s chairman. Bloomberg's Nathan Dean joins to discuss how Trump's push to reinstate Huang could effect the upcoming hearings.

items.headline: Anthropic Dips Below IPO Price in Sharp Tech Reversal
items.excerpt: Anthropic PBC shares sank 8% below their $83 initial public offering price, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week. Bloomberg's Carmen Reinicke joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: HPE Forecast Trails Top Estimates, Shares Fall on AI Growth Outlook
items.excerpt: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. shares dropped the most in more than six years after investors feared that continuing component costs will cut into the hardware company’s profitability next year despite rising revenue.
